Paper: [arXiv:2207.12598](https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.12598)

## Problem 

Generative models suffer from a fundamental trade-off: sampling diversity and sampling fidelity.
If the model samples from the entire probability space, it is highly diverse but noisy at the same time. 
To tackle this, researchers tried to narrow the model’s choice during the inference.


## Past attempts

- Low temperature sampling on discrete output distribution
  After logits are produced from the final layer of the neural networks and fed to the soft max for the normalisation, every logit is divided by T to increase the final score. 
  The probability distribution becomes sharper, i.e., only high probability terms are dominant. 

- Truncation trick on continuous input latent space
  When the vectors are mapped to a latent space, they form their own probability space with their own mean. 
  Truncation trick is to cut off the outer probability space away from the mean.

Above two methods are not suitable for multi-step models like diffusion.
For each step, noise is dampened, and the network has lower variance than the true data distribution.
Hence, the model goes to OOD. 

- Classifier guidance
  In order to guide the path of noisy states, external classifier is introduced.
  During training, both the diffusion model, and a classifier are trained in separate paths.
  Classifier here should be trained from scratch, as it should get noisy inputs rather than clean data.

While this method works for diffusion models, there are some downsides especially due to training two separate models.
One is that training two models and optimise them for the same goal is not simple.
This usually ends up adversarially.
Another is that classifier requires accurate labels and they are expensive. 

## Proposed solution

Instead of training two separate models, this paper suggests classifier-free guidance, which uses a single model.
During the training, the model uses the conditioning dropout, which is randomly throwing away the condition (e.g., prompt) and swapping that part with the null token.
At the inference, the single model is queried twice, with and without conditions dropped, and subtracts the outputs.
In this way, the model is guided to the condition.

## Limitations
After all, querying the model twice leads to additional computation costs.
The author also mentioned that guidance methods sacrifices sampling diversity over fidelity, and whether that is acceptable.
